passages.title: Passage I (Questions 1–5)
passages.body:
China’s government announced on April 19 that it had signed a landmark security pact with the Solomon Islands, evoking concern from Australia and the US. The agreement is the first of its kind that China has agreed with any country, and underlines its ambitions to play a security role in the Pacific. The final version has not been made public. It will pave the way for China to deploy its security forces there. The Solomon Islands can request police and military personnel “to assist in maintaining social order”, while China can make ship visits and use its ports for logistics. This will give China’s vessels a strategic foothold in the Pacific, in a region close to Australia and Guam, where the US has a naval base. Both countries unsurprisingly expressed concern, with Washington, even dispatching a senior official to the Solomon Islands, who will take up the pact as well as plans to reopen the US Embassy there.

The significance of the pact extends beyond the immediate regional security concerns in the Pacific. The Solomon Islands government said the agreement does not imply China will build a base there. The pact does, however, relate to a second key pillar of China’s avowed “peaceful rise” doctrine, which was, as popularised by “Panchsheel” or the “five principles of peaceful coexistence” — the “non-interference” in the internal affairs of other countries. The deployment of security forces in a foreign country certainly does not square with that idea. China has already begun to do so elsewhere, albeit on a limited scale. China’s past commitments on military bases and non-interference were intended to show the world Beijing would not seek to become a global “hegemon”, its favoured term to describe the US.
passages.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 6–10)
passages.body: Among the major objectives of the Glasgow Summit was to frame the foundation of an international carbon trading system listed in the Paris Agreement to achieve the target of net zero emissions by 2050. It would enable nations to transfer credits to each other and offset their emission targets. Critics of the trading system, and there are many, say it would give leeway to developed countries and companies that are highly polluting to stave off making deeper cuts in their low emissions by buying credits from poorer countries at exploitative prices. There are also major differences over whether the new trading system will recognize historical emissions permitted under earlier protocols. Others want rules that permit double credits for the nation funding a particular carbon reducing project, such as the regeneration of forests to act as a carbon sink, and for the country implementing it. A third issue is whether a share of the revenue from such a bilateral trading agreement will go toward the UN’s Adaptation Fund. There have also been concerns about the integrity of the accounting system for such credits.
passages.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage III (Questions 11–15)
passages.body:
The RBI expects inflation at 6.7 percent in 2022–23. Recent government data also suggests that inflation has become more broad-based. Excluding the volatile components such as food and fuel, core retail inflation was around 7 percent in April with almost all subgroups in the index witnessing elevated inflation. And considering the inflation in the pipeline — the wholesale price index continues to be in double digits — price pressures are unlikely to dissipate in the immediate term. According to analysts, while manufacturing firms have been passing on the rise in input costs, it remains incomplete in the case of the services sector. However, as demand firms up, the pass through is likely to gather traction. This combination of factors suggests that inflation may not fall dramatically as and when commodity prices fall — prices may prove to be a tad sticky on the downside. The RBI’s revised quarterly forecasts for inflation also seem to suggest so — inflation has now been projected at 7.5 percent in the first quarter, and 7.4 percent in the second quarter, trending downwards thereafter to 6.2 percent in the third quarter, and 5.8 percent in the fourth quarter.

Implicit in these quarterly inflation forecasts is also the acknowledgment that inflation will likely exceed the upper threshold of the central bank’s inflation targeting framework for three consecutive quarters. Considering the risks that the ‘unanchoring’ of inflation and inflation expectations pose to macroeconomic stability, and the country’s growth prospects, the central bank must look beyond its quotidian responsibilities and continue to focus on maintaining price stability, attaching primacy to inflation management.

Life has been thrown ______ due to the weather conditions in the city.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Thrown out of gear' means disrupted.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Had he told me the news beforehand, I ______ careful and saved my money.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Had he told me' is an inverted past perfect, so the result clause takes 'would have been'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He feels that he has been ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Taken for granted' means not properly appreciated.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He has the ______ touch of a maestro.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A maestro’s touch is smooth and skilful, so 'silken'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He is one of the ______ in the country.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'One of the' takes a plural noun. 'Well-renowned' repeats the same idea twice.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The population of Mumbai and Delhi is greater than ______ city in India.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A comparison of two cities against the rest of a class takes 'any other' plus a singular noun.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Perspicacity’ and ‘Perspicuity’
questions.opt_a: Perspicacity means ability to discern and Perspicuity means lucidity of expression
questions.opt_b: Perspicacity means lucidity of expression and Perspicuity means ability to discern
questions.opt_c: Perspicacity means tenacity and Perspicuity means lucidity of expression
questions.opt_d: Perspicacity means ability to discern and Perspicuity means tenacity
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: Perspicacity is sharpness of insight, and perspicuity is clarity of expression.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Complaisant’ and ‘Complacent’
questions.opt_a: Complaisant means overconfident and Complacent means in the same place
questions.opt_b: Complaisant means eager to please and Complacent means overconfident
questions.opt_c: Complaisant means eager to please and Complacent means in the same place
questions.opt_d: Complaisant means overconfident and Complacent means eager to please
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: Complaisant means willing to please, and complacent means smugly self-satisfied.
Step 2: Of the options, (b) is the closest, since complacent means overconfident or smug.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Compliment’ and ‘Complement’
questions.opt_a: Compliment means to enhance and Complement means to praise
questions.opt_b: Compliment means to go well with and Complement means to praise
questions.opt_c: Compliment means to praise and Complement means to go well with
questions.opt_d: Compliment means to enhance and Complement means to go well with
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: To compliment is to praise. To complement is to go well with and complete.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Deify’ and ‘Defy’
questions.opt_a: To deify means to confer upon one the status of God and to defy means to oppose
questions.opt_b: To deify means to confer upon one the status of God and to defy means to deny
questions.opt_c: To deify means to oppose and to defy means to confer upon one the status of God
questions.opt_d: To deify means to oppose and to defy means to deny
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: To deify is to make a god of someone. To defy is to resist openly or oppose.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Evoke’ and ‘Invoke’
questions.opt_a: Evoke means to elicit a response and Invoke means to provoke
questions.opt_b: Evoke means to call upon through an appeal and Invoke means to elicit a response
questions.opt_c: Evoke means to provoke and Invoke means to call upon through an appeal
questions.opt_d: Evoke means to elicit a response and Invoke means to call upon through an appeal
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: To evoke is to call up a feeling or response. To invoke is to call upon through an appeal, such as a deity or a law.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Sympathy’ and ‘Empathy’
questions.opt_a: Sympathy means sharing another’s feelings and Empathy means understanding another’s feelings
questions.opt_b: Sympathy means expressing another’s feelings and Empathy means sharing another’s feelings
questions.opt_c: Sympathy means pitying another’s feelings and Empathy means emphasising another’s feelings
questions.opt_d: Sympathy means emphasising another’s feelings and Empathy means pitying another’s feelings
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: Sympathy is pity or sorrow for someone, and empathy is entering into another’s feelings.
Step 2: (c) is the closest option, since it gives 'pitying' for sympathy. 'Emphasising' appears to be a misprint for 'empathising'. Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Accept’ and ‘Except’
questions.opt_a: Accept means to exclude and Except means to agree
questions.opt_b: Accept means to agree and Except means to extend
questions.opt_c: Accept means to agree and Except means to exclude
questions.opt_d: Accept means to extend and Except means to agree
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: Accept means to agree or receive, and except means to exclude.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Reward’ and ‘Award’
questions.opt_a: Reward is compensation for effort and Award is prize for recognition
questions.opt_b: Reward is prize for recognition and Award is compensation for effort
questions.opt_c: Reward is prize for recognition and Award is gift from someone
questions.opt_d: Reward is gift from someone and Award is compensation for effort
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: A reward is given in return for effort or service, and an award is a prize that recognises achievement.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Emigrate’ and ‘Immigrate’
questions.opt_a: Emigrate means to illegally go to another country and Immigrate means to arrive at another country
questions.opt_b: Emigrate means to arrive at another country and Immigrate means to leave for another country
questions.opt_c: Emigrate means to leave for another country and Immigrate means to illegally enter a country
questions.opt_d: Emigrate means to leave for another country and Immigrate means to arrive at another country
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: To emigrate is to leave one’s country, and to immigrate is to come into another.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that gives the correct meanings of both the similar-sounding words.

‘Immolate’ and ‘Emulate’
questions.opt_a: Immolate means to sacrifice and Emulate means to follow someone out of admiration
questions.opt_b: Immolate means to burn and Emulate means to wear ornaments
questions.opt_c: Immolate means to burn and Emulate means to simulate
questions.opt_d: Immolate means to destroy and Emulate means to imitate
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match each look-alike word to its own meaning.
Step 1: To immolate is to kill as a sacrifice, and to emulate is to imitate in order to match or surpass someone out of admiration.
Step 2: (d) is weaker, because 'destroy' is too broad.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__It would be nice to have__ (a) __a good evening stroll__ (b) __after five hours of office.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The idiom is 'hours in the office' or 'at work', not 'hours of office'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong. Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Arun likes__ (a) __Geography more than__ (b) __he likes History.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The comparison is complete and correct.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__While the solar energy has grabbed the spotlight,__ (a) __wind power too has been made steady progress__ (b) __across the world and in India.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Has been made steady progress' mixes the passive with an object. It should be 'has been making' or 'has made' steady progress.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong. Part (a) also has an unneeded 'the' before 'solar energy', so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Pride brings a__ (a) __great dealing of vanity,__ (b) __an egotistic inflation.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The idiom is 'a great deal of', not 'a great dealing of'.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Persuasion happens only__ (a) __when someone takes a stand__ (b) __from which he has unwilling to move.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Has unwilling' is ungrammatical. It should be 'is unwilling'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The food consumed__ (a) __is converted on__ (b) __the body into glucose.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: Food is converted 'in the body' into glucose. 'On' is wrong.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__This testing method requires__ (a) __one to fast overnight after which__ (b) __the fasting blood sugar level is measured.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The sentence is grammatical and clear.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Multiple research studies__ (a) __have laid emphasis on the importance__ (b) __of walking to improved glucose control.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: After 'to' meaning purpose, a base verb is needed: 'to improve glucose control'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__This also allows__ (a) __individual writers__ (b) __to play his strengths.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Individual writers' is plural, so the pronoun should be 'their', not 'his'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__As a screen writer,__ (a) __there are, broadly speaking,__ (b) __two kind of jobs in the film world.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Two' needs a plural noun, so 'two kinds of jobs'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

He headed the Indian freedom struggle __which__ paved the way for non-violent struggle for other countries in the 20th century.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Which' refers back to 'struggle' and joins the clause, so it is a relative pronoun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Where__ there is peace for some time, there will be prosperity.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Where' here shows place or situation and does not ask a question, so it is a (relative) adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Alas__ ! We have been defeated.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Alas' is an exclamation of sorrow, so it is an interjection.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

A zero is a __zero__ always.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Zero' names a thing, so it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

May you be blessed with __all__ good things of life.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'All' here points to the whole set of good things. It is normally a determiner, which is not offered, and of the options only 'pronoun' is close.
Step 2: Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The lake is one of the more __beautiful__ ones in the country.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Beautiful' describes 'ones', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Honesty__ is the best policy.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Honesty' is an abstract noun that cannot be counted, so 'uncountable noun'.
Step 2: 'Common noun' is also true in a broad sense, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

There is many a slip __between__ the cup and the lip.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Between' is followed by the noun phrase 'the cup', so it is a preposition.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Ravi and Megha reached first, __but__ Guha and Saavi finished third.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'But' joins two clauses of equal rank, so it is a (coordinating) conjunction.
Step 2: 'Connector' is a looser term for the same job, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

He is __the__ most sought after teacher in the school.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'The' is the definite article, a determiner.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2022 English set A (set code FDGT-F-ENG – A)
